title: The publican (Luke 18:9–14)
hookLine: O God, be merciful to me a sinner, and he went home justified

lines: AT LEAST I'M NOT LIKE THEM.
TWO MEN GO UP TO PRAY.
cards: Luke tells us who this story is for before he tells it: some people who trusted in themselves as just, and despised others. That's not a description of one group.
It's a habit, and it can belong to anybody: the scrolling that ends with at least I'm not like them. Two men go up to the Temple to pray at the same time. One is a Pharisee, careful and devout.
The other is a publican, a tax collector, the kind of man the first one looks down on.

teach.h: I AM NOT AS THE REST OF MEN.
teach.b: First the Pharisee. The parable isn't a verdict on Pharisees as a whole, and this one is genuinely devout.
He says: "O God, I give thee thanks that I am not as the rest of men", and then the list: not extortioners, unjust, adulterers, nor even like this publican. I fast twice in the week.
I give tithes of all that I possess. Those are real practices, and real discipline. The trouble isn't what he does.
It's the comparison: he's praying with one eye on God and one eye on the man in the back. Now the publican. He stands far off and won't even lift his eyes to heaven.
He strikes his breast and says: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." No list, no comparison, no excuses. Just the truth and a request.
And Jesus says: "this man went down into his house justified rather than the other." Justified means set right with God.
Then the line we heard at the dinner table: everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he that humbles himself shall be exalted. The publican's prayer has had a long life.
At Mass, during the Confiteor, people strike their breast, an echo of his gesture.

teach.h: O GOD, BE MERCIFUL TO ME A SINNER.
teach.b: And the Catechism links his cry, and the blind man's, to the Jesus Prayer, prayed in the East and the West: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.

how: At the Confiteor near the start of Mass, Catholics strike their breast, and some pray the Jesus Prayer, built in part on the publican's words, slowly with the breath; Eastern Christians may pray it on a prayer rope.

games.why: eight words and a struck breast. Jesus says this man went home justified rather than the other.

practice: Let your eyes lower, the way his did, and notice if your mind starts making a list, of your good deeds or of other people's faults; let the list go.
If you pray, say his words slowly with your breath, O God as you breathe in, be merciful to me a sinner as you breathe out; if you don't, simply sit with honesty about yourself, without comparing.

wordCard.voice: The publican. The tax collector at the back of the Temple who prayed eight words without comparing, and went home justified. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: be merciful to me, from the word family of atonement and the mercy seat.

carryVoice: Your line: be merciful to me. Eight words of his, still in use. See you tomorrow.
